findings.original_quote: HENT har nå signert kontrakt med Nscale for å utvide datasenteret med to bygg, med en samlet kapasitet på 75 MW. (Translation: HENT has now signed a contract with Nscale to expand the data centre with two buildings, with a combined capacity of 75 MW. No contract value is given in either language.)
findings.why_not_priced: The contract value was never disclosed and it was filed as a non-regulatory release, not inside information, so no number exists for the market to price; if it were priced, consensus intake would be visible and the stock would have reacted on 2 Sep (it did not move materially). Inference on the value, so small.

findings.finding: HENT's Narvik data-centre client Nscale is under public strain: Bloomberg (15 Oct 2026) reported its Norwegian flagship (Glomfjord, not HENT's site) six months late with penalties owed to Microsoft and ByteDance, and investors pushing back on its IPO valuation, so the Q3 call may draw counterparty-risk questions on HENT's Kvandal exposure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no prior counterparty-risk episode on this name
findings.why_not_priced: It is macro-to-company transmission: no Norwegian Sentia coverage linked the two, and the Kvandal project is separately bank-financed (USD 790m from DNB, Nordea, SEB et al., May 2026), so the market may rightly ignore it; sized small for that reason. If priced, Sentia would have traded down on 15-16 Oct; it fell from 80.1 to 79.4 on 14-15 Oct on heavy volume (329,805 shares), ambiguous.
findings.independence: Nscale Narvik financing: https://www.intelligentcio.com/eu/2026/05/12/nscale-secures-us790-million-for-norway-ai-data-centre-buildout/ (cuts the other way)
